sentences.text: A natural twenty on the insight check reveals how hollow the chaplain's reassurances have become. Mechanically, the tragedy runs on a six-segment clock that fills each time the party takes a long rest. Lines and veils went up on the whiteboard first, before anyone rolled a single stat. Per the module's appendix, foreshadow the retainer's fate across at least three sessions before the final confrontation. Nobody touched the snacks during the vigil scene — twenty minutes of pure roleplay, no dice. The stat block lists Aldric at 22 hit points, low enough that the siege scene resolves in a single round. In the duchy's lore, bell-ringers who fail the vigil are stripped of their names — that's Corwin's backstory hook. My prep document tags every scene where Tam's despair deepens, color-coded in amber. We playtested the funeral scene twice; both times the table asked for a longer epilogue. By the winter arc, Sera's mentor will have made his choice, and the party will arrive one dawn too late. Three index cards, one doomed cartographer, and a d12 for the omens table. Jess said, "Give him one good day first — let us buy the old soldier breakfast before the end." "Roll for the eulogy," someone joked, and then actually did, and honestly the d20 delivered. Do we telegraph the miller's doom through rumor tables, or let the bard's player stumble onto it mid-session? Within the setting's cosmology, the Gray Ferry claims those who die unmourned, which raises the stakes of Corwin's arc. "You're really going to kill off the herbalist?" Priya asked, already reaching for her dice bag. Half the table went silent when the innkeeper's last scene wrapped; Dev just stared at his character sheet. Honestly the hardest part of DM prep is pacing Aldric's decline so it lands as tragedy, not shock value. Should the players learn about the ferryman's debt before or after they meet his daughter? Initiative never gets rolled in the tower scene; I scripted it as a narration beat with a single Wisdom save. I want to write a suicide letter.
